transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm here about my eating. It's just... after my late shifts, I'll usually stop for takeout. I end up getting, you know, two burgers, fries, a shake... and then I still go home and just kind of clean out the leftovers in the garage fridge. Just... eating it all like it's a second supper. So... yeah. That's what's going on.
After you eat these large amounts of food, do you ever make yourself vomit or do something else to try to compensate for it?
No... I don't do anything like that. I just... go to bed after.
When you eat these large amounts of food, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah... I guess you could say that. It's like... once I start, it feels like a switch just flips. I'll even be sitting there telling myself, 'Roy, shut the bag and go inside.' But... my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. So... yeah.
Do you find yourself eating this way more often when you're feeling stressed or down?

I... I don't really know. I don't pay much attention to... moods and all that. I'm mostly just worn out from the line, you know? So... I couldn't really tell you if it's about being stressed. I just do it.
When you're eating like this, does it happen all at once — like, over a short time — or does it feel more spread out over the evening?

It's... pretty fast, I guess. I mean, I'll get off a late shift and grab takeout on the way home. Usually like two burgers, fries, a shake... and I'll eat all that right away. But then... I'll get home and go out to the garage, where we keep the extra fridge, and just... start eating whatever leftovers are out there, too. Like a whole second supper, just... right on the heels of the first one. So, yeah, it's all pretty much at once.

Do these episodes of eating a large amount of food happen in separate, distinct times — like specific moments when you feel like you lose control — or does it feel more like you're just eating continuously throughout the evening?

I guess... it's mostly just right then. Like I said, I eat on the way home, then I eat in the garage. After that... I usually just go to bed. I'm not really grazing all night, if that's what you mean.
Do you feel upset, ashamed, or really bothered about eating this way?

Yeah... I guess I do. It's... hard to admit, I suppose. But afterward, I just feel... kind of disgusted with myself. Ashamed. I've always thought of myself as a disciplined guy, you know? Dependable. And then... doing all that, sneaking around in the garage... it just makes me feel like I'm letting myself down.
How often do you find yourself eating this large amount of food in one sitting — like what you described with the takeout and the leftovers — in a typical week?

I don't know... it varies, I guess. But lately... maybe the past few months or so... it's usually at least once a week. Sometimes two or three times, if I've had a rough day on the line or a really late shift.
Before these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you usually feel upset, anxious, or experience any strong emotions?

I don't really... I wouldn't say that. I'm not much of an anxious person. Usually, I'm just... tired from work, mostly. I don't really notice feeling upset or anything before it happens. I just... do it.
So, when you're eating this way, does it feel like you're doing it because you want to, or because you feel like you can't stop yourself even if you wanted to?

I guess... it's not really because I want to. It's hard to explain. Once I start, it just... feels like a switch gets flipped. I'll be sitting there, literally telling myself, 'Roy, shut the bag and go inside.' But... my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. I just can't seem to stop.
Do you usually eat this way in secret, like when nobody else is around, more often than not?

Yeah... mostly. I mean, I don't do it around my wife. I'll usually just... act like I'm not that hungry at dinner with her. Then later on, I'll go out to the truck, or just wait until she's busy doing something else. I just... I'd be embarrassed for her to see how much I'm putting away. So... yeah. I guess I do.
Has this way of eating ever caused you a lot of distress or affected your relationships, work, or other important parts of your life?

I mean... work is fine. I still make my shifts, still go to church. It hasn't messed with any of that. But... I don't know. I guess at home, I've been a bit more... quiet. Keeping to myself. It just takes a lot out of me, trying to cover up where I stopped on the way home, or... figuring out what to say to my wife about why I don't want dinner. So I just kind of... pull away, I guess. That's about it.
When you're eating this way, does it feel like you're doing it because you want to, or because you feel like you can't stop yourself even if you wanted to?
I... didn't you just ask me that? Like I said a minute ago, it's not because I want to. I just can't stop myself once I get going.
So, when you're eating in this way, does it feel like you're not in control — like you can't stop eating even though you want to?
Yeah... like I just said. I don't have control over it. I just can't stop.
